items.title: No more ‘who shouts the loudest’: How Aldi decided where to spend on sustainability
items.summary: Supermarket chain Aldi Süd is known as a sustainability leader, in part through its decision to hold tight to its emissions reduction targets even as it pursues ambitious growth plans in the U.S. and U.K. What’s less clear is whether it can meet those climate goals.

items.title: Why automated product carbon footprints aren’t yet ‘decision-grade’
items.summary: Just a few years ago, creating a product carbon footprint (PCF) — an estimate of net greenhouse gas emissions over the product’s lifecycle — was an arduous process requiring weeks or months spent searching for relevant data.

items.title: How Meta applies emissions certificates to its disclosures
items.summary: Meta is placing bets on emerging environmental attribute certificate (EAC) schemes that support new technologies aimed at decarbonizing thermal energy, data center construction and freight, part of an initiative the company started three years ago .

items.title: More than 800 UK businesses could face review of renewable electricity tariffs under new rules
items.summary: # More than 800 UK businesses could face review of renewable electricity tariffs under new rules New research has found that 842 UK-headquartered organisations could be affected by new corporate climate reporting requirements that will place greater scrutiny on claims of using 100% renewable electricity.

items.title: COP31 ends without agreement. What does it mean for businesses?
items.summary: # COP31 ends without agreement. What does it mean for businesses? COP31 has ended in Antalya without an overarching political agreement on fossil fuels and climate finance.

items.title: IEA: Global energy efficiency set to grow 3% in 2026
items.summary: # IEA: Global energy efficiency set to grow 3% in 2026 With the Iran War flattening demand growth and progress accelerating around energy efficiency, global primary energy intensity is expected to improve by nearly 3% this year.

items.title: Electrification survives COP31’s failure to agree
items.summary: # Electrification survives COP31’s failure to agree Antalya's collapse is a blow to confidence in the COP process, but the economic case for electrification holds across geopolitical divides, argues We Mean Business Coalition's director of policy and strategy, Gillian Nelson.

items.title: Apply now: Entries open for the edie Awards 2027
items.summary: # Apply now: Entries open for the edie Awards 2027 The UK’s largest corporate sustainability awards scheme is celebrating its 20th year with a restructured programme, built around three pillars and new categories including AI, water and adaptation.
